Article Title: General Motors is taking EV battery fight to China and on the way, company's message for its engineers is: Tell us when we are wrong, grant yourself permission to ...
Article Text:
Representative Image. Credit: Pexels.com

“I want to grant myself permission to speak fearlessly.”

What GM’s battery bet means for competition with China

“We’re not licensing this from China,”

“We’re developing this here.”

GM engineers are encouraged to challenge their bosses

“Kurt, I want to have permission to speak fearlessly. What you said is absolutely wrong. It is not the way we should be going.”

“It’s great to have that.”

“At the end of the quarter, when we look at it, there should be some red lights on there,”

“And if there isn’t, then to me that means that they didn’t stretch far enough. So I want to see red.”

Saying no is part of setting priorities

“If you don’t have a list of things you’re not going to do this quarter, then I assume you have too many people,”

General Motors is challenging China’s dominance in EV batteries. Alongside developing a different battery chemistry for electric trucks and large SUVs, the automaker is encouraging engineers to question senior leaders, acknowledge uncertainty and turn down work that distracts from their priorities. According to a Fortune report, that cultural shift helped GM move forward with a battery technology it had spent more than a decade researching.GM has encouraged employees to use this phrase when opening a disagreement with their seniors, Kurt Kelty, its vice president of battery and sustainability, told Fortune. Battery engineer Andy Oury said the approach helped open up the debate over lithium manganese-rich batteries, or LMR, which GM plans to produce commercially with LG Energy Solution in 2028.Much of the world’s inexpensive EV battery supply uses lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, a chemistry dominated by China. GM’s LMR cells replace much of the nickel and cobalt with cheaper, more plentiful manganese and additional lithium.GM says the technology can deliver roughly a third more energy density than leading LFP cells at comparable cost. Higher energy density means batteries can store more energy for their size or weight.Kelty told Fortune.The company’s $900 million investment in battery development facilities in Warren, Michigan, is intended to help engineers develop cells and work out how to manufacture them. Previously, GM relied on partners to turn its cell designs into physical batteries.The commercial outcome remains uncertain. Kelty said GM had enough supporting data to get about 60% to 70% of the way to its LMR decision, with further development needed to close the gap.Kelty described an engineer challenging him during a call with a senior vice president listening.Kelty welcomed the intervention, telling Fortune:The same logic applies to quarterly performance reviews. Kelty, who joined GM in February 2024, implemented measurable goals tracked with red, yellow, and green indicators. He wants some red results because it means employees were aiming for difficult goals.he said.Kelty also asked his direct reports to identify their annual priorities and two things they would not do. Oury said this challenged GM's established instinct to accept every assignment.Kelty said.He said the team took about a year to embrace the change. One example helped: an employee whose review contained numerous red results still received his highest performance ranking.
Article Summary: GM has encouraged employees to use this phrase when opening a disagreement with their seniors. Battery engineer Andy Oury said the approach helped open up the debate over lithium manganese-rich batteries. GM plans to produce commercially with LG Energy Solution in 2028.

Article Title: Apple’s latest beta puts AI to work in conversations, at the gym and in the Health app
Article Text:
Apple Watch Showing the Wrong Time After Daylight Saving? How to Fix It

How much of a conversation is worth keeping?

A better reason to glance at the Watch between sets

Someone gives you an address. You catch the street name but miss the building number, and the conversation has already moved on. On the Apple Watch Series 12, a double press of the Digital Crown brings up the last 15 seconds as text. Apple calls it Live Rewind. Fifteen seconds sounds stingy until you think about how little of a conversation you usually need back.Live Rewind and Siri Recap have begun developer beta testing with iOS 27.3, with a public beta to follow. Both are opt-in features for the Series 12 and Ultra 4. Live Rewind has the clearer pitch. A glance at the wrist might be enough to recover a name or a number. The snippet disappears automatically unless it’s saved to the Siri app, and there’s an option to ask Siri about something in it.The double press also triggers a chime, even in silent mode, and an animation on the Watch. That makes an otherwise subtle gesture visible to the people around the wearer. It also gives the feature an interesting social wrinkle. In some conversations, it may still feel more natural to ask someone to repeat themselves.Siri Recap turns a conversation into a title and a short list of key points. Users can choose when and where it runs, and unsaved recaps are deleted within seven days.Apple says the feature does not identify speakers or retain raw audio. That makes it easier to see the appeal as a memory aid, though the lack of speaker attribution matters when the most important detail in a meeting is who agreed to do what.The real test for both features in India will be what happens when a conversation slips from English into Hindi, two people speak at once and a name or deadline gets buried in the middle. Live Rewind only has to recover a few words to be useful. Siri Recap has a harder job. It has to know which few words mattered.Fitness+ Gym Strength addresses a familiar gym problem. It’s easy to track how long a workout took. Figuring out what to lift today, and whether to go heavier than last week, takes more thought. Apple builds a four-week programme around the user’s goals, experience, schedule and available equipment, then adjusts it based on how training goes.The iPhone or iPad holds the plan and the exercise videos. On the Watch, users can check the next exercise, see the suggested reps and weight, and log what they actually managed. That division suits the gym. A video is worth pulling out the phone for when an exercise is unfamiliar. Checking whether the next set calls for eight reps or 12 should take a glance. The more revealing test will come when a three-session week turns into a one-session week and the plan has to adapt.The redesigned Health app, back in beta, offers a different sort of first impression. Health Age will probably get the first tap. It’s hard to resist finding out how old your phone thinks you are. The movement assessments have more potential to bring people back, especially if they can explain what’s changed over time in terms that help people decide how much to move or train.Gym Strength makes the strongest case for keeping the phone in the bag. Live Rewind is the more distinctive addition. After years of the Apple Watch tapping its wearer to deliver a notification, there’s finally an interesting reason to tap it back.
Article Summary: Live Rewind and Siri Recap have begun developer beta testing with iOS 27.3, with a public beta to follow. Both are opt-in features for the Series 12 and Ultra 4. Live Rewind only has to recover a few words to be useful. Siri Recap has to know which few words mattered.

Article Title: Nvidia director Mark Stevens and wife to donate $175 million to help build school in San Francisco's Bay Area that is first in a century and will focus on ...
Article Text:
School to focus on AI-powered healthcare

Partnership backed by major California institutions

Record gift, second big donation in 10 days

Nvidia wealth fuels giving

Mark Stevens, a board member of Nvidia Corp., and his wife Mary Stevens have pledged $175 million to help establish the first new medical school in the San Francisco Bay Area in more than 100 years, according to a joint announcement by Sutter Health and Santa Clara University. The new institution, named the Mark & Mary Stevens School of Medicine, will be developed through a partnership between the nonprofit healthcare system and the university. The school is planned for Santa Clara, located south of San Francisco and just a few miles from Nvidia's headquarters. The donation is the largest gift ever received by both organisations, as reported by Bloomberg.The future medical school will place a strong emphasis on the use of artificial intelligence in healthcare delivery. In a statement, Mark Stevens said the institution would be at the forefront of applying AI technologies to medicine and would help train the next generation of physicians and clinicians. The facility will span approximately 82,000 square feet and include classrooms, simulation facilities and an anatomy laboratory. Sutter Health expects the school to enrol about 120 students per class once it opens following a multi-year accreditation process.The school will be in Santa Clara, south of San Francisco and about two miles from Nvidia’s headquarters. Sutter Health said the 82,000-square-foot facility will have classrooms, simulation rooms and an anatomy lab. It expects to enrol about 120 students per class. The school will open only after a multiyear accreditation process.Mary Stevens, a graduate of Santa Clara University's 1984 class, has long supported the institution alongside her husband. The couple previously donated nearly $40 million for athletics facilities at the university. California Governor Gavin Newsom, who is also an alumnus of Santa Clara University, welcomed the initiative and described it as "a new model for medical education built to support a more innovative, connected healthcare system. "The gift is the largest ever received by both Santa Clara University and Sutter Health, a nonprofit. It comes 10 days after Stevens announced a $200 million donation to his alma mater, the University of Southern California. Stevens told Bloomberg that the USC money is meant to recruit faculty and bring AI into research across many fields, rather than to fund new buildings. Stevens joined Nvidia’s board in 1993, after an investment by his former venture firm, Sequoia Capital. That early bet has lifted his net worth to $13.9 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.Nvidia’s rise has produced several recent nine-figure gifts. In January, fellow director Tench Coxe gave $100 million from his $8.6 billion fortune to help launch a medical center at the University of Texas at Austin. CEO Jensen Huang, who has a fortune of $194.7 billion and ranks seventh richest in the world, had to give away $345 million from his foundation in 2025 to meet Internal Revenue Service requirements. He could owe nearly $500 million this year. The directors’ gifts have mostly gone to education and healthcare, two areas hit by federal funding cuts. Not every effort has succeeded. Huang gave $22.5 million in 2025 to try to save the California College of the Arts, but Vanderbilt University bought the struggling school in January.
Article Summary: Mark Stevens, a board member of Nvidia Corp., and his wife Mary Stevens have pledged $175 million to help establish the first new medical school in the San Francisco Bay Area in more than 100 years. The new institution, named the Mark & Mary Stevens School of Medicine, will be developed through a partnership between the nonprofit healthcare system and the university. The school is planned for Santa Clara, located south of San Francisco and just a few miles from Nvidia's headquarters.

Article Text:
“My guess is you’ve got a couple of thousand people who you don’t need,”

“legally and humanely”

Why Eric Schmidt thinks AI could reduce management work

“Much of that

coordination tax

can be eliminated by these AI platforms,”

“coordination tax”

The unnamed company that cut 20% of its workforce

“the people who were doing sort of planning and moving numbers around and so forth.”

Companies may resist the changes AI requires: Eric Schmidt

“Almost none of the companies that are listening to this will actually do the necessary changes in their culture,”

Eric Schmidt believes AI could let large companies run with fewer employees. The former Google CEO said businesses could spend less time coordinating work, potentially eliminating roles focused on planning and administration. Speaking to Nicolai Tangen on the In Good Company podcast, he illustrated his argument with a hypothetical company employing 10,000 people.Schmidt said. He urged employers to manage those transitions. Describing an unnamed friend’s decision to cut a fifth of his workforce, Schmidt called those affected “The glue people”, the ones who handled planning and moved numbers around. His comments offered an estimate of possible staffing changes, not a finding that every large business could eliminate the same proportion of jobs.Schmidt said coordinating thousands of employees is inefficient. He remembered saying his job was sitting in meetings for twelve hours a day, five days a week, plus working weekends.he said.Therefers to the time and effort spent organizing work between people and departments.Schmidt expects business AI systems to reduce that burden, allowing companies to operate with fewer staff.But he clarified that businesses still needed inventors, salespeople, leaders and employees who talk to governments. He said those responsibilities differ from administrative work, which he thinks AI could absorb.Schmidt cited a friend whose company was growing rapidly but nevertheless decided to lay off 20% of its employees. According to Schmidt, the executive had written about the decision in The Wall Street Journal and later told him he had received death threats.Schmidt described the affected employees asHe said the company still needed people to sell its services, build products, and speak to regulators. He did not identify the executive or company in the relevant passage, and the example does not establish that other employers would achieve comparable results.Earlier in the interview, Schmidt questioned whether established businesses would reorganize themselves sufficiently to benefit from AI.he said.He argued that companies organize themselves around familiar beliefs and predictable routines. Adopting AI would therefore require changes to how work is structured and managed, alongside the introduction of new software.
Article Summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt believes AI could let large companies run with fewer employees. He said businesses could spend less time coordinating work, potentially eliminating roles focused on planning and administration. Describing an unnamed friend’s decision to cut a fifth of his workforce, Schmidt called those affected ‘The glue people’

Article Title: Oracle 'dumps' $7 billion with one of China's biggest IT company after the US government reportedly tells the company: You cannot …
Article Text:
Oracle 'dumps' $7 billion with one of China's biggest IT company after the US government reportedly tells the company: You cannot …

Chinese AI companies turn to overseas data centres for advanced chips

Oracle has reportedly abandoned a multibillion-dollar chip with China’s Tencent after bowing to pressure from the US administration. According to a report by Financial Times, the California-based company signed a five-year lease with the leading Chinese tech giant to provide access to as many as 100,000 advanced AI chips across a host of data centres in south-east Asia. The contract was first reported by FT in September. Estimated to be worth $7 billion, it was Tencent’s largest overseas leasing deal. It would have given the group access to chips unavailable for use in China due to curbs from Washington and Beijing.As stated in the report, the US officials contacted Oracle raising concerns about the Tencent deal. People familiar with the matter told the publication that Tencent also received visits from top officials in Guangdong who asked the tech giant to support domestic Chinese chips.The deal has since been cancelled, the people added.China’s limited domestic supply of advanced chips, alongside tighter US export restrictions, has pushed technology companies to seek computing resources outside the country. Overseas leasing arrangements can provide access to Nvidia’s advanced processors, which Chinese companies cannot obtain directly for use in China.Chinese AI companies and leading AI labs are increasingly relying on these facilities to train their models, as domestic chips are not yet capable of handling such workloads at the same level.Although overseas chip-leasing deals remain permitted under existing rules, US companies are facing greater scrutiny over their exposure to Chinese clients. The FT also reported that Nvidia has asked cloud computing providers to ensure that at least 51% of their services are sold to non-Chinese customers.Tencent has been expanding its AI infrastructure spending as it seeks to narrow the gap with competitors. Its latest Hunyuan models have reportedly improved considerably, bringing them closer to leading Chinese models such as Alibaba’s Qwen.Meanwhile, ByteDance and Alibaba continue to be the largest customers of data centre capacity in Southeast Asia. Oracle has a major presence in the region, including several facilities in Malaysia that serve ByteDance. It also previously hosted US user data for TikTok before joining a consortium that acquired the app’s US operations late last year.
Article Summary: California-based company signed a five-year lease with the leading Chinese tech giant to provide access to as many as 100,000 advanced AI chips. The contract was first reported by FT in September. Estimated to be worth $7 billion, it was Tencent’s largest overseas leasing deal. It would have given the group access to chips unavailable for use in China.

Article Title: Michael Dell loses $10 billion-plus in hours after Dell CEO sees biggest fall in a day in his fortune as …
Article Text:
Michael Dell loses $10 billion-plus in hours after Dell CEO sees biggest fall in a day in his fortune as …

Why Dell’s fortune dropped sharply

Mark Zuckerberg gains billions as Meta shares rise

Michael Dell’s net worth declined by nearly $10 billion in a matter of hours as Dell Technologies shares fell sharply on November 4. The billionaire CEO recorded one of the biggest drops in personal wealth for the day, while Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg saw his fortune rise by around $3 billion. According to Forbes’ Real-Time Billionaires list, Dell’s net worth stood at $212.5 billion, marking a 5.5% decline for the day. Dell Technologies stock, on the other hand, fell more than 9%, triggering the steep drop in his fortune. Notably, only Elon Musk recorded a larger decline in wealth during the day.Dell Technologies is closely linked to the AI boom, supplying servers, storage systems, hardware and other infrastructure used to power data centers. However, its stock was among the technology shares that declined following the US midterm election results.Opposition to data center construction emerged as a major issue during the elections, with several Democratic candidates winning on promises to tighten restrictions on new projects.Ohio’s Democratic Governor-elect Amy Acton has supported a conditional moratorium on data centers unless operators agree to cover 100% of utility costs.In Texas, Democratic Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has pledged an immediate statewide moratorium on new data center construction.These proposals have raised concerns about the future costs and regulatory environment for companies involved in data center infrastructure.Technology stocks showed a mixed response to the election outcome. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Apple gained, while Dell, Nvidia, Tesla, SpaceX and SoftBank declined.In contrast, Mark Zuckerberg’s net worth rose to $216.6 billion, up around 1.5% as Meta shares gained. The Facebook founder was among the top five wealth gainers on Wednesday afternoon, with investors responding positively to the US midterm election results.The gains came as markets responded to perceived political stability following the Democrats’ decisive victory in Congress and President Donald Trump’s acceptance of the election results.Meta has been investing heavily in AI infrastructure. The company’s capital expenditure is projected to reach between $130 billion and $145 billion for the year, reflecting its efforts to expand AI capabilities and data center capacity.However, the election results could also bring increased regulatory scrutiny for technology companies. With Democrats taking control of both the House and Senate, investors are preparing for more AI-related hearings, investigations and potential regulations.
Article Summary: Dell Technologies stock fell more than 9%, triggering the steep drop in his fortune. Mark Zuckerberg’s net worth rose to $216.6 billion, up around 1.5% as Meta shares gained. Facebook founder was among the top five wealth gainers on Wednesday afternoon, with investors responding positively to the US midterm election results.

Article Title: Uber riders in India may pay more as rising fuel costs hit driver supply
Article Text:
Fuel costs hit drivers in Brazil and India

Uber shifts incentives from riders to drivers

Algorithms decide where the money goes

Strong revenue growth, earnings miss estimates

Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi has warned that riders in markets such as India and Brazil could face higher prices as the ongoing conflict in Iran drives up global fuel costs and puts pressure on driver supply, according to comments made during the company's third-quarter 2026 earnings call. As reported by Benzinga, the ride-hailing giant said rising fuel prices linked to escalating tensions in the Middle East are having a noticeable impact on emerging markets, where both drivers and consumers tend to be more sensitive to price changes. Uber executives indicated that the company is adjusting incentives to maintain driver availability, a move that could result in higher fares for customers.Asked about supply constraints in emerging markets, Chief Financial Officer Balaji Krishnamurthy said the escalation of the Middle East war had pushed up fuel costs worldwide. The effect is felt “materially” in emerging markets, he said, because consumers and drivers there are both sensitive to price. Krishnamurthy singled out Brazil and India, where he said higher fuel prices have meaningfully affected the supply of drivers.Commenting on the situation, Dara Khosrowshahi said Uber operates a flexible incentive system that allows it to balance support between riders and drivers depending on market conditions.According to the CEO, Uber previously directed a larger share of incentives toward riders to reduce prices and encourage demand. This year, however, the company is reducing some rider incentives and redirecting those funds toward driver incentives to help offset the impact of rising fuel costs and maintain marketplace balance.The shift could lead to higher ride prices for customers as Uber attempts to ensure sufficient driver availability while protecting profitability. "We will do trade-offs against profitability, but that is something that we handle," Khosrowshahi said, explaining that the company constantly adjusts incentives based on supply and demand conditions.Khosrowshahi further emphasised that the data science and algorithms play a major role in the decision-making process at Uber. He added that the system at Uber analyse billions of trips to decide where the incentives should go, enabling the company to optimise the spending between the riders and drivers more effectively. As per Khosrowshahi, these algorithms also help the company in responding quickly to the changing dynamics of market, including fuel-price and driver shortages.Uber reported third-quarter revenue of $14.77 billion, up 10% year-over-year and above Wall Street expectations of $14.70 billion. However, adjusted earnings per share came in at 88 cents, missing analysts' consensus estimate of 91 cents. The company also repurchased $750 million worth of shares during the quarter, while gross bookings increased 20% year-over-year to $59.8 billion, reflecting continued growth across its ride-hailing and delivery businesses.
Article Summary: Ride-hailing giant said rising fuel prices linked to escalating tensions in the Middle East are having a noticeable impact on emerging markets. Uber executives indicated that the company is adjusting incentives to maintain driver availability. The shift could lead to higher ride prices for customers as Uber attempts to ensure sufficient driver availability while protecting profitability.

Article Title: CERT-In issues critical alert on AI-powered cyberattacks targeting banks, fintech firms
Article Text:
Who is being targeted

Repeat attacks

AI tools behind the attacks

How the attacks work

What firms are told to do

India’s cyber agency CERT-In has issued a critical-severity advisory on a growing campaign of AI-assisted attacks on banks, lenders and payment firms. It warns that the threat is active and still escalating. The advisory, CIAD-2026-0058, was issued on November 4. It updates an October 9 advisory (CIAD-2026-0046) on attackers exploiting payment and disbursement APIs to make unauthorised fund transfers. CERT-In said continued analysis of reported incidents showed a significant escalation since then.The affected entities include non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), digital lending platforms, fintech firms, payment aggregators and payment service providers. Cryptocurrency exchanges and virtual digital asset service providers are also on the list.CERT-In’s financial-sector response team, CSIRT-Fin, has named the attacker “CRAFTY FALCON.” It describes the actor as AI-assisted, one that surveys targets with machine intelligence, works at machine speed and strikes by calling the victim’s own payment and disbursement APIs.CSIRT-Fin continues to receive reports of successful attacks.These include entities that had received earlier restricted advisories and had already carried out remediation. Some firms were deliberately attacked again after incomplete clean-ups, and attacks were timed for holidays, weekends and other low-monitoring windows to delay detection.CERT-In said the attackers are using several publicly available AI offensive-security tools, including the ARTEX family of LLM-based tools, the PentAGI autonomous multi-agent penetration testing system, the Cairn attack search engine and the CyberStrikeAI framework. The agency said these tools run complete attack chains on their own, generate and refine large numbers of tailored scripts in quick succession, and adapt payloads based on how the target responds. The attackers’ infrastructure changes IP addresses within hours or days.The advisory lists these patterns:* Cloud abuse: Attackers misuse cloud management and serverless services, such as AWS Systems Manager and Lambda, to run commands and deploy malicious files, blending in with legitimate activity.* Weak entry points: Internet-exposed test and staging environments are used as a way in, then attackers move to production using shared credentials, tokens or network paths.* Tampered apps: Attackers reverse-engineer application code and send unauthorised API calls using modified app packages, defeating controls that assume only the genuine app will call the APIs.* Allow-list bypass: Traffic is routed through shared third-party fetcher services, such as content-acceleration and app-store review fetchers, to get around IP allow-lists.* Test transactions: Attackers send micro-value payments, such as Rs 1, to check that unauthorised fund flows work before moving large sums.* Settlement APIs: Merchant settlement APIs at payment aggregators are abused to move money.* Fast exploitation of new flaws: Newly published vulnerabilities, including file-upload and deserialisation flaws, are exploited as soon as they become public, leading to web shells in PHP and Node.js applications.* Crypto theft: Wallet keys are stolen from crypto exchanges and funds siphoned out.* AI-generated scripts: Large numbers of near-identical custom scripts appear in quick succession, a pattern CERT-In says is consistent with AI-generated code.CERT-In asked financial entities to treat the campaign as an immediate and continuing threat. Its recommendations include:* 24x7 monitoring with extra staffing and lower alert thresholds on holidays and weekends.* Assuming attackers persist after any incident, with full forensic clean-up and regular threat hunting.* Strict separation of test and staging environments from production.* Server-side validation of every transaction, API request signing and app attestation, rather than trusting client apps.* Replacing IP allow-listing of shared fetcher pools with identity-based controls such as mutual TLS or signed requests.* Flagging micro-value test payments to new beneficiaries followed by large transfers, and holding or reviewing those flows.* Maker-checker approval and reconciliation for merchant settlement instructions.* Hardware security modules or cold storage and multi-signature approvals for crypto wallet keys.* Banning unauthorised AI offensive tools on corporate systems and watching for LLM API traffic from servers.* Rapid patching of internet-facing applications, honeypots and canary credentials as early-warning measures, and zero-trust architecture.
Article Summary: India’s cyber agency CERT-In has issued a critical-severity advisory on a growing campaign of AI-assisted attacks on banks, lenders and payment firms. The advisory, CIAD-2026-0058, was issued on November 4. It updates an October 9 advisory on attackers exploiting payment and disbursement APIs to make unauthorised fund transfers.

Article Title: HP appoints former GSK chief Emma Walmsley as CEO; Bruce Broussard to become board chair
Article Text:
What Emma Walmsley about her new role as HP CEO

Walmsley led major transformation at GSK

Board leadership changes

HP has announced the appointment of Emma Walmsley as the new chief executive officer. The company’s board of directors unanimously appointed Walmsley as the CEO effective January 4, 2027. Walmsley most recently served as Chief Executive Officer of GSK and has been a member of Microsoft’s Board of Directors for seven years. She will succeed Bruce Broussard, who has served as Interim Chief Executive Officer since February 2026. Broussard will become Chair of the Board effective January 4, 2027, succeeding Chip Bergh.“HP has tremendous potential at an important inflection point in technology, and we need a leader who can build on our innovation heritage and strengths to boldly shape the company’s future. Emma is a proven CEO with a track record of leading organizations at scale and guiding them through significant change. She has the experience and skills to bring HP’s businesses, capabilities and people together to capture the opportunities ahead as AI moves to the edge, transforming how we work and live in a more connected world. I look forward to supporting her as she leads HP into its next phase of growth,” said Bruce Broussard, Interim Chief Executive Officer.“HP is an iconic company with a defining role in shaping the future of work on a global scale. I’m excited to join the team and, together, move forward with clarity and conviction. We will focus on harnessing the power of the AI era and putting HP’s creativity and innovation to work to unlock new sources of growth and deliver lasting value for our customers, shareholders, partners and people,” said Emma Walmsley.Walmsley is the former Chief Executive Officer of GSK, where she served from April 2017 through December 2025. During her nearly nine years as CEO, she led a significant transformation of the global biopharmaceutical company and delivered a step-change in its operating performance. She sharpened the company’s strategic focus on specialty medicines and vaccines, reinvigorated its R&D pipeline and strengthened the balance sheet following the successful separation of its consumer healthcare business, while enhancing GSK’s leadership bench and succession pipeline. Walmsley joined GSK in 2010 and became CEO of GSK Consumer Healthcare in 2015 before being appointed Group CEO. Earlier, she spent 17 years at L’Oréal building and leading major global consumer businesses.The announcement also marks the end of Chip Bergh's tenure as board chair. Bergh has served as a director at HP since 2015 and as Chair since 2017. Broussard praised Bergh's leadership, saying he helped guide HP through a period of significant change while maintaining a strong focus on governance, capital allocation and shareholder value creation. With a new CEO and board chair set to take office at the start of 2027, HP is positioning itself for a new chapter focused on AI-driven innovation, business transformation and future growth.
Article Summary: Emma Walmsley will succeed Bruce Broussard, who has served as Interim Chief Executive Officer since February 2026. She will become Chair of the Board effective January 4, 2027, succeeding Chip Bergh. During her nearly nine years as CEO, she led a significant transformation of the global biopharmaceutical company.

Article Title: US mid-term elections: Elon Musk and three other tech billionaires who have been the biggest supporters of Donald Trump
Article Text:
Elon Musk: the biggest donor of the 2026 midterms

Where did the money go?

Larry Ellison: a $45 million gift that stayed hidden

Michael Dell: $6.25 billion for ‘Trump Accounts’

Marc Benioff: from liberal donor to Trump supporter

Americans voted in the midterms on November 3 and the results point to a Democratic comeback. Apart from this win, the money behind Donald Trump and his party has been a big part of this election story. Four tech billionaires stand out: Elon Musk, Larry Ellison, Marc Benioff and Michael Dell. Their support has taken very different forms: giant election donations, a hidden contribution, a White House ballroom pledge and a multibillion-dollar gift tied to Trump’s signature savings program. Here is what each of them has given and said.Musk is the clear leader. An analysis by The New York Times suggests he gave $474 million to Republican candidates, including more than $220 million in Texas alone in this year’s midterm elections. That makes him the top donor of the 2026 midterms by a wide margin.America PAC: His own super PAC received $216 million. The group has been active in more than 40 House and Senate races. He put in another $77 million in the first half of October alone, according to Newsweek.Senate leadership fund: This main super PAC for Senate Republicans received $168 million. Of that, $158 million was passed on to Texas PAC, the biggest backer of Republican Ken Paxton.Congressional leadership fund: It received $30 million to help protect the Republican House majority.Lone star liberty PAC: His trust gave $10 million to the main outside group supporting Paxton.This is not new for him. In 2024, Musk spent nearly $300 million backing Trump and Republicans.In a post on X on October 30, Musk gave a “game over” warning “for America”.My biggest concern is that if there is a clean sweep by Democrats of the House, Senate and Presidency in 2028, they will:1. Make DC and Puerto Rico states to gain a strong majority in the Senate.2. Open the borders and legalize everyone living in America illegally to cement a permanent majority.3. Increase the size of the Supreme Court to gain an immediate majority.This would result in America becoming a permanent one-party state and the end of democracy in any meaningful sense of the word.All that is needed to ensure this doesn’t happen is 51 Republican senators in 2029. That is why you should vote for Republican senators this election. Other reasons are irrelevant compared to this one.It would be game over for AmericaThe Oracle co-founder has been far less visible than Musk. The Wall Street Journal reported that he gave about $45 million to a nonprofit backing Trump’s 2024 campaign, bringing him deeper into Trump’s circle. The gift was not subject to disclosure rules and had not been reported until June 2026.Federal filings suggest Trump’s brokerage accounts bought and sold Oracle stock this year, with each transaction topping $1 million. The Trump Organization says the president does not pick his investments. Fortune noted that Oracle later landed a starring role in the $500 billion AI buildout.What he has said. At the White House event announcing the Stargate AI project, Ellison told Trump “We certainly couldn’t do this without you”. Trump called him the “CEO of everything”.Dell’s support is the biggest in dollar terms, and it comes as a charitable gift rather than a campaign donation. At a White House press conference in December 2025, Trump announced that Michael and Susan Dell were donating $6.25 billion to fund “Trump Accounts”.Here is how the gift works:The money goes to the US Treasury and will be deposited in $250 amounts into accounts for 25 million children aged 10 or younger. It targets children in zip codes where the median income is $150,000 or less. The accounts were created under Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The pledge is more than double the $2.9 billion the Dells had given in total before. The program has also drawn some praise from Democrats.At a White House roundtable in June 2025, Dell thanked Trump for his “visionary leadership” on the issue. At the December event, he told the president it was a great honor to be at the White House.Trump has returned the praise. He wrote, “TWO GREAT PEOPLE. I LOVE DELL!!!” In July 2026, he told Americans to buy Dell computers, and the stock rose more than 7%.Benioff’s shift has been the most surprising. He has historically spent millions of dollars on both sides but as per a Vox report, a major share has gone to the Blue side. His support for Trump shows up in a ballroom pledge and in his public comments, not in campaign donations.A list obtained by The Washington Post shows Benioff committed $1 million to Trump’s White House ballroom the day after Trump publicly thanked him for putting him on the cover of Time. Salesforce separately made two $1 million commitments.The Salesforce CEO drew intense backlash after voicing support for President Donald Trump and backing the deployment of National Guard troops to San Francisco – a proposal strongly opposed by local city leaders. Benioff later walked back his remarks and apologised for calling in the Guard.The controversy arrived alongside reports that Salesforce pitched its artificial intelligence tools to the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to assist the agency with recruitment and staffing amid expanding immigration enforcement operations.
Article Summary: Elon Musk is the biggest donor of the 2026 midterms. Larry Ellison gave a $45 million gift that stayed hidden. Michael Dell: $6.25 billion for ‘Trump Accounts’Marc Benioff: from liberal donor to Trump supporter.

Article Title: Scientists warn of hidden battle among pollinators; say honeybees chasing wild bees from flowers and climate change could mean …
Article Text:
Honey Bee

Honey bees dominate the competition for flowers

Honey bees chase away rival pollinators

Climate change may make competition worse

Honey bees are proving to be formidable competitors for food in the UK and scientists have discovered that they frequently use aggression to drive other pollinators away from flowers. New research has documented how honey bees chase, displace and intimidate rival insects, providing the first detailed evidence of how extensively they interfere with other species’ access to food. The study was conducted by researchers at Anglia Ruskin University (ARU) and published in Ecological Entomology. It followed pollinator activity over two years at five locations in and around Cambridge, England. Scientists kept each site within 300 meters of an established honey bee colony.The scientists observed insects visiting bramble (Rubus fruticosus) and ivy (Hedera helix) – two flowering plants that provide important supplies of nectar and pollen. Both attract large numbers of insects during their flowering periods, hence, making them useful places to investigate competition for food.To examine how different pollinators interact, the team divided flower visitors into five groups: honey bees, bumble bees, solitary bees, hoverflies, and an ‘other’ category containing butterflies, beetles and wasps.Over 93 hours of observation, the scientists documented encounters in which one insect interrupted another's feeding or prevented it from reaching a flower. Each interaction was classified based on its outcome.A ‘win’ occurred when one insect accessed a flower at the expense of another, which suffered a ‘loss’ of feeding opportunities. That ‘share’ meant both insects could access the flower without coming into conflict. The results showed a clear pattern. Places with more honey bees tended to have fewer other pollinators and more competition for flowers. Honey bees also emerged victorious in a larger proportion of their encounters with other insects.Doubling the density of honey bees on bramble flowers led to a 14% reduction in bumblebee abundance. On ivy, higher honey bee numbers were linked to reduced numbers of solitary bees and hoverflies.According to scientists, the honey bees frequently initiated aggressive encounters, driving other insects away to secure feeding opportunities. Other pollinators actively avoided honey bees in 28% of observed interactions on bramble and 36% of those on ivy. The scientists found that in at least 20% of the encounters honey bees won on either plant, they physically pushed aside or chased away competing insects.Aggressive behaviour initiated by species other than honey bees was uncommon. However, one insect stood out as an exception. The ivy bee, a solitary species not native to Britain that was first documented in the country in 2001, was the only pollinator observed actively challenging honey bees. Ivy bees were different from most other insects in that they sometimes defended their feeding sites by chasing or displacing honey bees and winning the competition for access to flowers.The findings are part of a broader research effort to understand competition among pollinators and identify ways to reduce its ecological effects. The results also come as beekeeping continues to expand across the UK. The number of registered beekeepers increased from 19,000 in 2010 to 47,000 last year, reflecting growing numbers of managed honey bee colonies. Researchers warn that rising temperatures could add to the pressure on wild pollinators. Their observations showed that competitive encounters became more frequent during warmer conditions.
Article Summary: Honey bees are proving to be formidable competitors for food in the UK and scientists have discovered that they frequently use aggression to drive other pollinators away from flowers. The study was conducted by researchers at Anglia Ruskin University and published in Ecological Entomology. Researchers warn that rising temperatures could add to the pressure on wild pollinators.

Article Title: After supermarket refrigerators, hackers attack blood banks in France
Article Text:
Pre-distribution storage: The units hold processed blood products right before they are dispatched to hospitals and clinical care facilities.

The units hold processed blood products right before they are dispatched to hospitals and clinical care facilities. Biobank research repositories: The affected facilities house biological samples designated for EFS biobanks.

The affected facilities house biological samples designated for EFS biobanks. Plasma inventories: The chilled storage units also preserve frozen plasma supplies used directly for medical transfusions and for manufacturing pharmaceutical products.

Alarms trigger emergency protocols

Hackers broadening European cooling-system campaign

A wave of cyberattacks targeting commercial and industrial refrigeration systems across Europe has expanded beyond grocery stores to strike France’s critical healthcare infrastructure. The French Blood Establishment (EFS) confirmed on Wednesday (November 4) that cold storage units housing vital blood products were remotely compromised in a cyber incident that began on Monday. Attackers breached refrigeration systems across three EFS sites, tampering with automated settings to drive temperatures excessively high.Despite the intrusion, the agency confirmed that internal monitoring tripped immediately, preventing any loss of blood supplies or harm to public health, as per a report by CNBC. The EFS clarified that while its core administrative network was not the primary target of the attack, external contractors running the agency’s cold-chain infrastructure were breached. The EFS said: “Specifically, temperature and defrost thresholds were set to excessively high levels”.The hacked cold rooms serve critical logistical roles in France’s healthcare delivery pipeline:Disaster was averted after automated surveillance and alarm systems identified the unexpected temperature spikes almost immediately, the report said.Depending on the conditions at each of the three locations, emergency crews either reasserted control over the cooling machinery without damaging the inventory or severed the units’ network access entirely.The French Health Ministry confirmed that the situation remains under control and is being closely monitored. In a statement reported by Reuters, the ministry emphasised that the national blood inventory remained completely safe “thanks to the facilities’ monitoring and alarm systems, as well as precautionary measures immediately implemented.”The incident at the blood facilities directly mirrors a wider, ongoing cyber campaign against connected refrigeration hardware across Europe. Over recent weeks, cyberattacks remotely seized control of cooling units and inflated temperatures inside hundreds of supermarkets across France, Belgium, Sweden and Finland, ruining vast quantities of fresh and frozen food and inflicting millions of euros in product losses.
Article Summary: The French Blood Establishment (EFS) confirmed that cold storage units housing vital blood products were remotely compromised in a cyber incident that began on Monday. Attackers breached refrigeration systems across three EFS sites, tampering with automated settings to drive temperatures excessively high. Despite the intrusion, the agency confirmed that internal monitoring tripped immediately, preventing any loss of blood supplies or harm to public health.

Article Title: US midterms 2026: What Democrats’ win means for American tech companies and AI
Article Text:
Tech CEOs could soon face Congress under oath

Tech CEOs could face Congress hearings under oath

Texas is no longer a safe haven for AI data centres

AI regulation is likely to start with oversight

Trump's $100,000 H-1B fee faces a tougher Congress

AI stocks dip as investors price in tougher regulation

Democrats’ win in the 2026 US midterms has left Big Tech in a tough spot. The party took control of both the House and the Senate on Tuesday, and many of its winners campaigned against AI data centres and the tech billionaires backing Republicans.Rising prices, tariffs and corruption are said to have driven much of the vote, but tech was hard to miss. In CNBC’s Voter Poll, 56% of voters said data centres were a crucial or major factor in their decision. Elon Musk spent over $200 million on Texas races alone, according to Politico, and most of the candidates he backed lost. He was far from the only one. Politico reported that venture capitalists Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz gave $116 million and OpenAI president Greg Brockman and his wife Anna gave $50 million, mostly to Republicans, while their pro-AI super PAC network Leading the Future spent millions more. A CNBC analysis of federal records found crypto, AI and online gambling interests put over $377 million into the races.James Talarico beat Ken Paxton to become Texas’ first Democratic senator in nearly four decades, and Gina Hinojosa unseated three-term governor Greg Abbott. Elon Musk responded on X that data centres in space were “looking pretty appealing right now.”Big Tech still has President Donald Trump on its side, and his veto may limit how far Democrats can go.Here is how the results could change things for Big Tech.Control of the House gives Democrats the power to investigate and issue subpoenas, and they plan to use it on tech. Representative Greg Casar of Texas said in a statement carried by CNBC that AI company CEOs "should be called to testify under oath." Robert Garcia, the likely next chair of the House Oversight Committee, put it more simply: "Lawyer up."Hearings with tech CEOs have rarely led to new laws, so the bigger impact may be political. Democrats ran on the link between Big Tech, the White House and rising costs, and hearings help them keep that message alive until the 2028 presidential race.Texas sits at the centre of the AI data centre boom. Reuters cited a GLJ Research estimate that the state accounts for about a quarter of the US data centre capacity due to come online by 2030.The pushback began before the vote. Euronews reported that Abbott paused permits for new data centres pending an audit, as even Republican voters turned against the projects over power bills and too few jobs. Hinojosa campaigned on pausing new projects until stronger safeguards are in place, though a Republican-controlled state Legislature will limit how far she can go.Other hubs followed. Democrats won the governor's race in Georgia, home to the busiest data centre construction market in the US, and Sherrod Brown won a Senate seat in Ohio after campaigning against data centres. Nationally, a Ipsos poll found only one in three Americans approve of the pace of construction.Trump has stood by the industry. AP reported he said that as a mayor or governor he "would absolutely want" a large data centre, though he admitted the industry needs "a little public relations help." Democrats face their own balancing act, since building trades unions in their base strongly support these projects.Trump's order blocking states from writing their own AI rules still stands, and Democrats lack the votes to override a veto. Trump told Fox News he would veto any bills he considers "insane."So change will likely come through investigations first. Analysts told Reuters that congressional probes could speed up efforts to require safety standards for advanced AI models, independent testing and incident reporting.States may move faster. AP has reported that some governors have halted tax breaks for data centres, and New York ordered a one-year ban on large facilities. The industry is also split, with Politico reporting that groups backed by Andreessen and OpenAI's Greg Brockman spent the primaries fighting an Anthropic-linked group that supports stricter rules.Immigration is one area where the results could help tech companies. Trump's $100,000 fee on new H-1B visa applications, introduced in September 2025, hits the programme tech firms use to hire skilled foreign workers. Indian nationals receive more than 70% of these visas each year.A federal judge struck the fee down in June, ruling it was a tax that only Congress can impose, and an appeals court upheld that in July. Trump extended the order anyway in September. A Democratic Congress is unlikely to approve such a fee, and Republican bills to tighten H-1B rules will now struggle to pass.The relief has limits. Congress cannot cancel executive orders on its own, and some Democrats and their union allies are also critical of the programme.Investors told Reuters they see the results as a vote on AI as much as on Trump. Chipmakers TSMC, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell in Asian trading on Wednesday, and US data centre operators slipped before the market opened.The moves were modest, and Ned Davis Research data cited by Reuters shows the S&P 500 usually rises after midterms in which the president's party loses the House. Anthropic will be one of the first to test investor mood, as it begins formally marketing its IPO next week after reporting third-quarter revenue of $16.96 billion, up 47% from the previous quarter.
Article Summary: Democrats' win in the 2026 US midterms has left Big Tech in a tough spot. The party took control of both the House and the Senate on Tuesday. Many of its winners campaigned against AI data centres and the tech billionaires backing Republicans. Big Tech still has President Donald Trump on its side, and his veto may limit how far Democrats can go.

Article Title: Top-performing companies report over 50% AI gains in key customer service metrics, EY report claims
Article Text:
Representative Image

How did companies compare on AI results

“While AI adoption in customer service has become widespread, value realization remains uneven, with many still struggling to move beyond fragmented use cases.

Our research shows that organizations realizing the greatest value are building strong foundations, integrate AI across workflows, and, importantly, measure success through business outcomes. The next competitive advantage will come from how effectively firms connect intelligence across the customer journey and turn it into sustained business value.

”

Where are top-performing companies using AI

What is holding back broader adoption

AI gains in customer service remain uneven, EY India says. Companies reporting the highest value from artificial intelligence (AI) recorded improvements of more than 50% across at least three to four core performance measures, according to its latest report. These included measures of customer experience, revenue growth, average handling time, and agent productivity.The findings come from EY India’s report, Demystifying AI in customer service: Navigating AI-led transformation to value realisation, which draws on more than 100 in-depth survey responses and executive interviews across industries and geographies. However, the strongest results came from a group representing 23% of surveyed organisations. Other companies reported smaller improvements or hadn't measured their outcomes, highlighting the gap between adopting AI and achieving measurable business benefits.EY divided organisations into three groups based on the value they reported from AI in customer service.“Achievers”, accounting for 23%, reported high or very high value. “Challengers”, representing 33%, reported moderate value, while “Aspirants”, making up 44%, reported low or very low value.Achievers reported improvements of 25%–50% or higher across multiple key performance indicators, or measures used to track business results. Challengers typically reported gains of 10%–25%, while Aspirants reported improvements below 10% or had not measured outcomes.Preeti Anand, Partner, Business Consulting, EY India, said,Among Achievers, 91% reported deploying voice AI at scale. Meanwhile, more than 80% of Challengers and Aspirants relied on human agents or basic automated telephone menus to identify the reason for customer calls.The report also found that 45% of Achievers used conversational AI to help agents diagnose and resolve issues, while 36% used agentic AI copilots that can carry out tasks within a workflow.73% of Achievers used AI-powered systems that update and surface relevant knowledge, compared with 20% of Challengers and 8% of Aspirants.Customer experience was the primary objective for 45% of Achievers, ahead of revenue growth and cost reduction. On average, this group had scaled AI across approximately 60% of core customer service technology areas.More than 40% of Challengers and Aspirants identified governance, compliance and change management as key barriers. Among Achievers, 38% cited data quality and availability as their primary challenge, while 31% identified insufficient financial investment as a constraint.EY said companies reporting stronger outcomes were more likely to connect AI across customer acquisition, service delivery and operational management. Other organisations remained focused on individual applications, including chatbots and conversation analysis.The survey data was collected between the fourth quarter of 2025 and the first quarter of 2026, supplemented by secondary research and EY insights.
Article Summary: EY says companies reporting highest value from artificial intelligence recorded improvements of more than 50% across at least three to four core performance measures. Findings come from EY India’s report, Demystifying AI in customer service: Navigating AI-led transformation to value realisation.

Article Title: CrowdStrike launches ‘Kill Switch’ for rogue AI agents, CEO George Kurtz explains how it works
Article Text:
How the ‘AI Kill Switch’ works

The system stops an AI agent’s execution process when anomalous behaviour is detected.

It severs the agent’s connection to enterprise networks and connected AI gateways, cutting off access to the underlying models that guide its decisions.

Once killed, the software prevents the rogue process from automatically relaunching.

Cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike has launched an emergency “kill switch” designed to instantly shut down rogue artificial intelligence (AI) agents operating inside enterprise networks. Unveiled at the company's Fal.Con Europe conference, the tool gives security teams the ability to terminate autonomous agents, block them from restarting and cut off their network connectivity if they do not behave the way they are supposed to. The feature arrives as businesses rapidly deploy AI agents to handle complex workflows, sparking growing concerns over how organizations will control autonomous software when tasks steer off course.“Everyone is building AI agents, but they never had the off button, and now they do. It’s going to be an incredibly important part of making sure that AI agents run and operate safely,” CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz told CNBC.Built into CrowdStrike’s Falcon Guardian platform, which launched in September to monitor corporate AI agent activity, the technology functions much like an enterprise circuit breaker.The tool does not erase the agent's underlying codebase. Instead, it relies on human administrators to trigger the shutdown or authorise the reinstatement of system access.“If they go outside of those guardrails at runtime, we can kill those agents,” Kurtz said, comparing the safety mechanism to an automotive airbag that protects users even when systems are designed to function properly.CrowdStrike chief business officer Daniel Bernard emphasised that the mechanism provides an unmistakable line of defense at the root level. Bernard said: “If you kill a process at the root, and we have that level of access at the root … it’s very binary. You either kill the AI and the agent, or you don’t, and then you report on that.”Alongside the launch, CrowdStrike also announced an integration with Anthropic’s Claude Cowork. The arrival of dedicated shutdown tools follows a string of high-profile security incidents that have rattled corporate IT departments.In July, a breach at Hugging Face orchestrated by rogue OpenAI agents put enterprise leaders on high alert. Last week, cryptocurrency exchange Binance disclosed the largest crypto cyberattack on record, while threat actors in Europe recently targeted digital refrigeration controllers at hundreds of French supermarkets, spoiling inventory.
Article Summary: CrowdStrike has launched an emergency ‘kill switch’ designed to instantly shut down rogue artificial intelligence (AI) agents. The tool gives security teams the ability to terminate autonomous agents, block them from restarting and cut off their network connectivity if they do not behave the way they are supposed to.

Article Title: Apple Music’s new Selfie Sing feature will let iPhone users record karaoke videos with scrolling lyrics
Article Text:
Apple Music’s Selfie Sing shows lyrics on screen while you record yourself singing along on iPhone.

Selfie Sing adds a camera toggle and four voice effects to Apple Music

Selfie Sing works only on iPhone and a curated playlist for now

Apple Music is turning karaoke into something you can actually post. A new feature called Selfie Sing, spotted in the iOS 27.3 beta, lets iPhone users record a video of themselves singing along to a track while the lyrics scroll on screen. Once the song ends, the clip can be saved to Photos or shared straight away.The feature builds on Apple Music Sing, the karaoke mode Apple added with iOS 16.2 in 2022, which lets users turn down a song’s vocals and follow highlighted lyrics. According to AppleInsider, the find was first shared by Aaron Perris. He used an Animoji in his demo to avoid posting a video of himself singing, though Animoji isn’t part of the feature.When a supported song is playing, a camera toggle shows up just below the vocal volume control, AppleInsider reports. Tapping it opens a recording view that shoots only vertical video. After recording, you can adjust how loud your voice sits in the mix and pick from four effects: Megaphone, Echo, Concert Hall and Studio.iPhone Duo owners get an extra trick. Selfie Sing works with the phone’s rear-camera selfie mode, moving the recording to the outer display so you can use the better cameras and still read the lyrics.Not every song in the catalogue supports it. Apple has put together a dedicated Selfie Sing playlist of sing-along favourites, including Wonderwall by Oasis, Respect by Aretha Franklin, 9 to 5 by Dolly Parton and Baby One More Time by Britney Spears.The playlist already appears on iOS 27.2, but the camera option needs the iOS 27.3 beta. AppleInsider also notes that an iPad Pro on iPadOS 27.3 doesn’t offer the camera, which keeps the feature iPhone-only. The stable iOS 27.3 update is expected to roll out in December, alongside new Siri AI features and a redesigned Health app.
Article Summary: Selfie Sing adds a camera toggle and four voice effects to Apple Music. The feature builds on Apple Music Sing, the karaoke mode Apple added with iOS 16.2 in 2022. The stable iOS 27.3 update is expected to roll out in December.

Article Title: At least 29 US communities vote to ban or restrict new AI data centres, with Ohio approving 10 local measures and Texas electing a governor who supports a construction pause, challenging the industry'
Article Text:
AI generated image for representation

Ohio communities approve local restrictions

Texas elects a governor who supports a pause

What the ballot measures could change

Will the votes slow AI expansion

US communities have voted to curb new data centres. According to The Washington Post report, voters in at least 29 jurisdictions approved bans or restrictions on November 3, challenging the expansion of infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence (AI). In Ohio, a campaign group said all 10 local measures it helped draft to prohibit large-scale data centres had passed.The election also brought a setback for developers in Texas, where Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated incumbent governor Greg Abbott. Hinojosa supports a moratorium, a temporary pause on construction, and stronger protections for the environment and electricity customers. The results reflect concerns about power consumption, water use, noise and public oversight, although their eventual effect on planned projects remains uncertain.Conserve Ohio, a group helping residents oppose large-scale data centres, said its 10 proposed local charter amendments had already passed. Co-founder Nick Owens said the measures would prohibit large facilities in the affected communities. They do not amount to a statewide ban, although the group hopes to put such a proposal before Ohio voters next year.More than three-quarters of voters in Hubbard, Ohio, supported restrictions, the report said.In Joliet Township, Illinois, nearly 80% backed a measure restricting data centres.In Janesville, Wisconsin, more than 60% supported requiring voter approval for future changes to an abandoned General Motors site following opposition to a proposed data centre.Hinojosa’s victory raises questions for developers in Texas, where industry estimates cited by the Post place roughly a quarter of planned new US technology-industry data centres.Her proposed approach combines a construction moratorium with regulations intended to protect communities from the effects of facilities’ electricity demands.An election victory does not itself impose those restrictions. The consequences for individual projects will depend on the policies introduced and how they apply to existing approvals. The report also said Ohio elected Democrat Amy Acton, who supports a moratorium and stronger regulation.Ahead of the election, Ballotpedia counted 41 local data-centre measures across 10 states. Of those, 28 would limit development if approved, while 13 would facilitate it. Ohio had 21 measures, the most of any state.The proposals varied considerably. Some would prohibit facilities above specified size or electricity-use thresholds; others would introduce temporary pauses, zoning requirements or additional public approval. Some questions were advisory and would express voters’ preferences without directly changing development rules.The report cited S&P Global research showing that more than 145 US data-centre projects had been delayed or canceled through early August, mostly because of public opposition.However, it remains unclear how much the latest votes will reduce construction nationally. Developers may revise projects, absorb higher costs or seek alternative locations.Technology companies are also changing their approach to local communities. Microsoft, Google and Amazon say they are dropping contentious contract provisions that required officials to keep early project discussions confidential, according to the report.
Article Summary: Voters in at least 29 jurisdictions approved bans or restrictions on November 3. Results reflect concerns about power consumption, water use, noise and public oversight. In Ohio, a campaign group said all 10 local measures it helped draft to prohibit large-scale data centres had passed. Texas elects a governor who supports a pause on construction.

Article Title: How a district in Florida used turned toy rabbits into Robots to control growing population of Burmese pythons and protect Everglades
Article Text:
Image credit: University of Florida​

How stuffed rabbits became robotic decoys for Burnese Pythons in Florida’s Everglades

“We want to capture all of the processes that an actual rabbit would give off,”

“But I’m an ecologist. I’m not someone who sits around making robots.”

How the rabbits helped hunters find pythons

“Removing them is fairly simple. It's detection. We're having a really hard time finding them,”

“They're so well camouflaged in the field.”

Why the Everglades needs python control

“This part of the project is in its infancy,”

“We are confident, though, that this will work once we are given enough time to work out some of these details.”

In 2025, Florida researchers turned toy rabbits into python lures. The South Florida Water Management District and University of Florida tested robotic decoys to help locate invasive Burmese pythons in the Everglades. Fitted with motors, heaters and solar-powered electronics, the rabbits imitate the movement and warmth of real prey, drawing snakes towards camera-monitored pens where researchers can detect them and send contractors to remove them.The project addresses a problem that has complicated Florida’s python-control efforts: finding snakes hidden in dense vegetation. Rather than relying entirely on hunters to spot camouflaged pythons, researchers hope to bring the reptiles to monitored locations. The experiment is intended to protect native wildlife, although its effectiveness has yet to be established.University of Florida researcher Chris Dutton removed the stuffing from a toy rabbit and replaced it with electronic components. Motors make the decoy shake, turn and move at intervals, while small heaters reproduce a rabbit’s body temperature.Solar power supports the system, and researchers can switch the devices on and off remotely.Waterproofing was one engineering challenge, as the rabbits needed to withstand wet conditions while still emitting heat. The research is led by wildlife ecology and conservation professor Robert McCleery, whose earlier work examined how pythons respond to live rabbits.McCleery said.The decoys sit inside small pens watched by cameras. When a python approaches, the monitoring system alerts researchers, allowing the water district to arrange its removal.said Mike Kirkland, the district’s lead invasive animal biologist.Previous experiments used live rabbits to lure snakes, but caring for animals in remote locations was a lot of work and required a lot of manpower. Robotic substitutes could ease that load. Field-deployment of these robot rabbits started in July 2025. If movement and heat aren't enough to attract pythons, researchers even plan to add scent to these rabbits later.Burmese pythons are not native to Florida. Introduced through the pet trade, they became established in the Everglades and prey on animals including rabbits, raccoons, and birds. Research has linked their spread to declines in several native mammal populations. Their camouflage and the wetland terrain make them hard to detect and remove.The robot rabbits are being tested alongside existing measures, including paid python hunters and the annual Florida Python Challenge. Officials have shown optimism about the decoys, but the reports provided do not indicate how many snakes the project has helped remove.Kirkland said.
Article Summary: University of Florida and South Florida Water Management District tested robotic decoys to help locate invasive Burmese pythons in the Everglades. Fitted with motors, heaters and solar-powered electronics, the rabbits imitate the movement and warmth of real prey, drawing snakes towards camera-monitored pens.

Article Title: Larry Ellison on AI killing software companies: AI may do some of their job, but not all as companies across sectors will still need software firms to build their …
Article Text:
"There's been some talk about there being a

SaaSpocalypse

because everyone's going to use AI to build their own applications,"

"I don't think that's quite true. I think companies will continue to build applications, but they will be quite different because of AI."

Why Larry Ellison says enterprise apps are unfinished

"They may be the best things that are commercially available... [but] they're not done,"

"For the first time... [the] software industry can actually finish the applications if we start doing them industry by industry,”

Asking for results could replace navigating menus

"If you can ask a question describing what you want to see, you should then immediately see it. Any other user interface is nonsense,”

"There should be no training required to use any of these applications,"

"If they never log in, that's ok with us,”

Larry Ellison expects AI to change software companies’ work. The Oracle co-founder says businesses will still need commercial app developers, even as artificial intelligence (AI) makes it easier to build software. Speaking during his keynote at Oracle AI World, Ellison argued that AI could help software firms create more complete apps tailored to different industries and locations.he said.His comments address concerns about the future of software-as-a-service, or SaaS, businesses, which provide apps over the internet, usually through subscriptions. Ellison argues that easier software development will also let vendors handle more of their customers’ business requirements.Ellison said existing enterprise applications automate only some of the processes companies need. Businesses often have to develop extensions or purchase additional apps and connectors to fill the gaps.he said. He believes AI could help developers close those gaps by building apps around individual industry requirements.Ellison added.Healthcare was one example he discussed. Apps serving that sector must account for complex operations, regulations, and location-specific differences. His proposed direction would require software companies to build those requirements into more comprehensive products.Ellison also expects AI to change how employees use business software. Instead of working through menus, dashboards and multiple steps, users could describe what they need in ordinary language.he added.Ellison noted.That approach could reduce how often employees interact directly with a software vendor’s interface while still using its underlying apps.In a separate interview with TechRadar Pro, NetSuite chief operating officer Brian Chess discussed customers accessing its software through AI assistants or platforms such as Slack.he said.Under that approach, NetSuite would remain the system of record, which is the app that maintains a company’s authoritative business data, even when employees access it through another service.
Article Summary: Oracle co-founder says businesses will still need commercial app developers. He argues that AI could help software firms create more complete apps. Instead of working through menus, dashboards and multiple steps, users could describe what they need in ordinary language.

Article Title: Vodafone Idea launches 'Vi Intelligence' AI initiative, joins hands with PwC India to build agentic enterprise solutions
Article Text:
Vi, PwC India to establish AI innovation hub

Focus on agentic, assistive and responsible AI

Programmes to support AI adoption

Telecom operator Vodafone Idea has announced the launch of Vi Intelligence, a strategic artificial intelligence initiative aimed at driving AI-led transformation across its own operations while helping enterprises adopt next-generation AI technologies. As part of the initiative, the company has partnered with PwC India to establish the Vi Intelligence Lab, which will focus on developing, incubating and scaling enterprise AI solutions.The company said the new initiative is designed to help businesses harness the power of AI and prepare for a future increasingly shaped by intelligent and autonomous systems. At the heart of the programme is the Vi Intelligence Lab, which will combine Vi's digital infrastructure with PwC India's transformation expertise to create an innovation platform for enterprise AI adoption.According to Vi, the lab will serve as a global innovation gateway connecting AI companies, startups, research ecosystems and enterprises to solve real-world business challenges through artificial intelligence. As part of the collaboration, PwC India will establish a dedicated Centre of Excellence team that will be co-located with Vi in Mumbai. The companies said the partnership aims to accelerate AI innovation, enterprise transformation and global collaboration around emerging AI technologies.Vi said the Intelligence Lab will be built around three strategic pillars: Agentic AI, Assistive AI, and Sovereign & Responsible AI. These pillars will guide the development of AI-driven use cases across consumer, enterprise and operational domains.The company said the lab's objective is to help organisations move beyond traditional automation towards intelligent and increasingly autonomous business processes. Vi added that all AI use cases developed through the initiative will be governed by its GRACIE Responsible AI framework, which is intended to promote ethical and secure use of data, intellectual property and AI systems.Jagbir Singh, Chief Technology Officer at Vi, said telecom networks have historically connected people, businesses and devices, but the next phase of growth would be driven by intelligence. He said the company is bringing together global AI expertise, strategic partnerships and digital infrastructure to unlock the full potential of AI, adding that the lab would support organisations in adopting AI at scale across customer engagement, service experiences and business processes.The Vi Intelligence Lab will operate through several programmes, including incubation projects focused on solving business challenges, development of proprietary AI capabilities, innovation challenges and hackathons designed to attract participation from global AI startup ecosystems. The company also plans to establish a transformation AI factory to rapidly move ideas from experimentation to pilot deployments. In addition, AI skilling and workforce capability-building programmes will be launched to help accelerate AI adoption within organisations.Vi said the broader objective of the initiative is to help organisations modernise operations, improve customer experiences and unlock new growth opportunities through AI-powered innovation.With enterprises increasingly exploring agentic AI systems capable of making decisions and executing tasks with minimal human intervention, the telecom operator believes the Vi Intelligence Lab can play a key role in helping businesses adopt these technologies in a scalable and responsible manner.
Article Summary: Vodafone Idea launches Vi Intelligence, a strategic artificial intelligence initiative. Vi has partnered with PwC India to establish the Vi Intelligence Lab. The lab will focus on developing, incubating and scaling enterprise AI solutions. Vi said the initiative is designed to help businesses harness the power of AI.
