Article Title: Why Texas turning Blue is Elon Musk’s ‘biggest defeat’
Article Text:
Elon Musk

How much Tesla CEO put in and why Texas matters to Elon Musk

My biggest concern is that if there is a clean sweep by Democrats of the House, Senate and Presidency in 2028, they will:

1. Make DC and Puerto Rico states to gain a strong majority in the Senate.

2. Open the borders and legalize everyone living in America illegally to cement a permanent majority.

3. Increase the size of the Supreme Court to gain an immediate majority.

This would result in America becoming a permanent one-party state and the end of democracy in any meaningful sense of the word.

All that is needed to ensure this doesn’t happen is 51 Republican senators in 2029. That is why you should vote for Republican senators this election. Other reasons are irrelevant compared to this one.

It would be game over for America

Texas is home turf for Musk and the tech world

What Musk said after the result

Musk’s influence on US elections

A bad night for big money

Some of the richest people in American politics spent heavily backing Republicans in November 3 elections but their side lost the Senate’s control. Nowhere did it sting more than in Texas where Democrat James Talarico beat Republican Ken Paxton for the Senate, even though Elon Musk spent a fortune to help Paxton, according to a New York Times analysis. Democrat Gina Hinojosa also won the governor’s race. For a state that has anchored the Republican map for over 30 years, it is a stunning turn. For Musk, who donated a total $474 million (nearly half a billion dollars) to Republican candidates, including more than $220 million in Texas alone in this year’s midterm elections, it is arguably his biggest political defeat.Musk was the largest donor of the 2026 midterms. Most of it went to his own America PAC and to the top super PACs for Senate and House Republicans. His biggest play was in Texas, his adopted home state and the headquarters of Tesla and SpaceX. In September alone, he gave $158 million to the Senate Republicans’ main super PAC, which was quickly routed to a super PAC backing Paxton, the state’s attorney general. America PAC also spent more than $47 million against Talarico. The New York Times put Musk’s total spending in the state at roughly $224 million.His reasoning was the long game. Musk has said Republicans needed a defence in case Democrats sweep Washington in 2028, and he feared they would grant statehood to Washington, DC and Puerto Rico.In a post on X on October 30, Musk gave a “game over” warning “for America”.Texas, with its cowboy hats, slow-smoked barbecue, favorable tax policies and fewer regulations, was supposed to be the antidote to California for tech people purportedly fed up with Silicon Valley’s Democratic politics. Other reasons Musk promoted Texas over California are relatively low-cost real estate and housing, and business-friendly environment.Musk helped build that image. He moved Tesla’s headquarters to Texas in 2021. In 2024, he moved SpaceX’s incorporation there from Delaware, after a Delaware judge invalidated his $56 billion Tesla pay plan. Musk said: “SpaceX has moved its state of incorporation from Delaware to Texas! If your company is still incorporated in Delaware, I recommend moving to another state as soon as possible.”He has also said SpaceX’s main office would move to Boca Chica and X would move to Austin. Many tech moguls came to Texas looking for redder politics. On Tuesday, the state turned a lot bluer.Elon Musk responded on X with jokes.“Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” he wrote, and then, “Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time.”Later he reposted conservative exit polling that showed Republican voters still backing the Trump administration’s immigration policies but seeing the war in Iran as a “losing issue.” His reply was one word: “Interesting.”The jokes follow a sharper tone in October, when he wrote, “Live by the sword, die by the sword,” and warned that he would find out who is “really pulling the strings.” An October report by Politico said that democrats are eyeing many targets, the biggest of them may be Elon Musk, as they make plans to probe corruption in and around President Donald Trump’s administration if they win control of the House next month.Musk’s returns have been uneven. In 2024 he spent over $290 million, mostly to help Donald Trump retake the White House, and later became the effective head of the DOGE office. In 2025 he and allied super PACs spent over $20 million on a Wisconsin Supreme Court race, and his favoured candidate lost by more than 10 points. With Texas now ‘Blue’, next up are the 2028 presidential primaries.Musk was not the only billionaire to come up short. In Ohio, Vivek Ramaswamy lost the governor’s race to Democrat Amy Acton after putting an estimated $36 million of his own money into it. In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms beat Republican billionaire Rick Jackson. In Texas, Governor Greg Abbott, who began the year with $105.7 million on hand, conceded to Hinojosa. According to the Associated Press, Democrats also won both the House and the Senate. Whether or not Texas is truly a battleground now, Republicans can no longer take its voters for granted.
Article Summary: Elon Musk was the largest donor of the 2026 midterms. Most of it went to his own America PAC and to the top super PACs for Senate and House Republicans. His biggest play was in Texas, his adopted home state and the headquarters of Tesla and SpaceX.

Article Title: WhatsApp may soon roll out new Shortcuts for Android and iPhone users: Here's how they are likely to work
Article Text:
How the new Message Text Actions feature of WhatsApp is said to work

Works with sent and received messages

What each shortcut does

Privacy remains unchanged

Availability

WhatsApp is reportedly rolling out a new feature which could make it easier for users to interact with the information shared in WhatsApp Chats, as reported by WABetaInfo. Available only to some select users, the feature called "Message Text Actions" or "Smart Text Actions," is designed to automatically detect details like phone numbers, dates, addresses and email IDs, then offers contextual shortcuts directly within conversations. As per the report, the feature is being introduced on both Android and iOS users of WhatsApp and is made to reduce the need to copy and paste information from other apps.The feature is created to automatically identify supported text formats within both incoming and outgoing messages. Whenever WhatsApp spots a phone number, date, address or email address in a message, it will automatically draw a dotted underline beneath that text. When the user taps on the underline a popup will appear on the screen that shows the text WhatsApp detected at the top. This will enable the users to check the text and make sure that the app picked the correct message. Users who don’t wish to use the shortcut can simply ignore it and can carry on with their conversation.One of the important aspects of this update is that the shortcuts are not limited to messages received from contacts.The feature also works for the messages sent by the user, as this will make it easier for the users to interact with the information which was already present in the previous conversation. The report further adds that WhatsApp will also display the detected text in a pop-up menu, enabling the users to verify that the app has identified the information correctly before they proceed with any action.* Phone numbers: Users can copy the number, add it to contacts or place a call through their phone carrier. For business numbers, they can also see the business’s information.* Dates and times: Users are able to add the date to their calendar, copy it or make a new event within WhatsApp.* Addresses: Users are also allowed to copy the address and open it directly in maps.* Email addresses: Users can also open the address in their mail app or copy it.WABetaInfo noted that some of these actions already existed, but WhatsApp is now making them easier to find and use.After a user picks an action, WhatsApp asks whether it was useful. If the user says it wasn’t, they can say whether the app detected the wrong text or the action wasn’t needed. WABetaInfo said this only sends WhatsApp a flag and not the message content. The tracker also said the detection happens entirely on the device, using pattern-matching rules, so WhatsApp never receives the message content or the suggestion. As a result, the feature does not affect end-to-end encryption.The feature is currently being rolled out to select users running the latest versions of WhatsApp on Android and iOS, with wider availability expected in the coming weeks.
Article Summary: WhatsApp is reportedly rolling out a new feature which could make it easier for users to interact with the information shared in WhatsApp Chats. The feature called "Message Text Actions" or "Smart Text Actions," is designed to automatically detect details like phone numbers, dates, addresses and email IDs. As per the report, the feature is being introduced on both Android and iOS users of WhatsApp.

Why did the entire police force in Milner resign

What Police Chief Lamar Bunn alleged about GPS tracker

The entire full-time police force of Milner, a small city in Georgia, has resigned amid a growing dispute with city leadership. According to a report by Fox News Digital, Milner Police Chief Lamar Bunn has accused the city manager of secretly placing a GPS tracker on his truck, while alleging that concerns over legal compliance and ethical conduct have affected his ability to continue in the role. The city manager, Tausha Grose, has also announced her resignation, officials said during a city council meeting last month. The developments have raised concerns over the future of the Milner Police Department, with officers calling for an investigation into the conduct of city leadership.In his resignation letter obtained by Fox News Digital, Bunn said he was stepping down because of fundamental differences with city leadership over governance, legal compliance and ethical standards.“I have determined that it is in my best interest to step down at this time due to fundamental differences regarding leadership, governance, and ethical alignment. Regrettably, recent actions and governance decisions within city leadership — specifically regarding legal compliance, ethical standards, and core values — have compromised my ability to perform my duties with integrity,” Bunn wrote.Milner Police Captain Craig Walton also called for an independent investigation into Mayor Craig Timmons.In his resignation letter, Walton urged residents and city council members to examine the mayor's conduct and possible violations of his oath of office or the rights of city employees.During the city council meeting, Tausha Grose announced that the full-time police department had resigned, along with most of its part-time officers. I don't know why. It's because I've devoted my life to Lamar County. 15, 16 years with the sheriff's office and now I'm back here in this county. My dad was here in '74 policing with his police department. I got roots here,” Bunn said.Mayor Craig Timmons acknowledged the concerns raised during the city council meeting and said he hoped the situation could be resolved.as the city works to address the concerns raised by its former officers and city manager.

Article Title: Google to everyone saying 'company threatened schools over using AI; says: We want to clarify, we are giving more …
Article Text:
Google to everyone saying 'company threatened schools over using AI; says: We want to clarify, we are giving more …

Here’s what Google said

We want to clarify what we announced today about our education services. Today’s announcements give schools more choice, not less. Here’s what we announced:

- Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search will be OFF 🔴 by default.

This is based on K-12 schools asking for more control over student use of AI services.

- Schools are in control: They can choose to turn ON 🟢 one, two, or all of these services individually.

- We are also updating Search for schools to make it better for learning. Specifically, AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don’t get quick answers to schoolwork.

We know there’s concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork, and schools have told us they want control.

That’s exactly why we are making these changes today to address the feedback we’ve heard from educators in recent months. And we’ll continue to engage deeply with educators to ensure we are giving schools more choice, more controls, and improved Search for learning.

Schools should have control over AI in classroom: Google

A report recently claimed that Google is turning off the AI tools – Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search for K-12 students starting next year. Google’s vice president of education, Chris Phillips, told The New York Times that the company’s AI features are “deeply integrated” into Search, meaning students cannot access one without the other. Soon after the announcement, many politicians and leaders including Bernie Sanders and New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani voiced their outrage on social media. “Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools,” Zohran Mamdani wrote on X (formerly Twitter). Bernie Sanders wrote that “Google is threatening schools,” referring to the policy as “extortion.”The company has now responded to the claims issuing the clarification on the change. “We want to clarify what we announced today about our education services. Today’s announcements give schools more choice, not less,” Google wrote on X.In the post, Google clarified that while Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search will be OFF by default, Schools will be in control. They can choose to turn ON one, two, or all of these services individually, the tech giant said.The company also published a blog post where it said that “schools should have control over AI in their classrooms and in providing administrators with controls to help them manage their approach”.“After listening to schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers, we are now updating our approach to controls for Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search. Access to these products will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on,” it said.“We’ll share more specifics with schools in the coming months ahead of the changes rolling out so they have time to prepare and enable a smooth transition. Our goal is simple: provide school leaders the control and confidence to use AI products in classrooms as they see fit.We’ll continue to listen to feedback and evolve our approach as we work in partnership with schools, teachers, pedagogical experts, and parents on helping the next generation learn and thrive”.
Article Summary: A report recently claimed that Google is turning off the AI tools – Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search for K-12 students starting next year. “Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools,” Zohran Mamdani wrote on X (formerly Twitter) Bernie Sanders wrote that ‘Google is threatening schools’ and referred to the policy as “extortion”

Article Title: After admitting 'hardest year' yet in its 13-year history, Canva announces major job cuts; CEO sends long 'layoff email'
Article Text:
CEO calls it Canva's toughest year

Canva layoffs : 22% of workforce affected

Support package for affected employees

Major organisational overhaul planned

Read Canva CEO Melanie Perkins’ email to employees here

Hi everyone,

Today, I have some profoundly difficult news to share.

After months of thinking through how to set Canva up for the next chapter, we have made the incredibly hard decision to make significant changes to how we’re organised, where some of our teams are based, and the roles and skills we need for the future.

This means 1,271 people, or 22% of Canva, will be impacted. For some people, this will mean changes to their roles or being asked to relocate to centralised hubs. Sadly, it will also mean saying goodbye to teammates and friends who have helped build Canva into what it is today.

This is without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history. Behind every decision is someone we care deeply about, and I know the consequences will be very real for those directly affected, their families, friends and teammates.

I’m deeply sorry for the pain and disruption this will cause for everyone affected. While nothing can make this news easier, we will do everything we possibly can to support everyone affected.

I want to explain as openly as I can why we're making these changes, how we reached these decisions, and, most importantly, how we will care for the people affected today.

Why we’re making these changes

We've spoken a lot about how quickly the world is changing. New technology is transforming what people can create, how they create it, and what they expect from the products they use.

Over the past thirteen years, we’ve turned a dream in a pitch deck into a platform used by hundreds of millions of people.

None of it would have been possible without the talent, imagination and care of every single person who has been part of this journey. Yet success in our first chapter doesn’t guarantee success in the next. This has been our hardest year yet, and as we shared earlier this year, our growth has slowed for the first time in a decade.

After exploring a wide range of alternatives, I've come to the difficult conclusion that small changes won’t be enough.

To set ourselves up for the next decade, we need to refound Canva, getting back to our roots of small, empowered teams with the freedom to make decisions, take ownership and focus on what matters most for our community.

It also means making some of the hardest decisions we've ever faced, including saying goodbye to people who have helped make Canva what it is today. For that, I am deeply sorry.

What we’re changing

We're making three changes to bring more of what has made Canva special back into how we work.

#1. We're simplifying how we come together to build Canva

As we've grown, more of our work has become organised around team structures and narrow areas of ownership. Improving one part of our product often requires navigating between Product, Growth and Platform, with more handovers and coordination than necessary. This has made it harder to take ownership of bigger problems and to build a deeply unified product for our community.

We’ve tried many ways to solve this over the years, but it’s become clear we need to revisit our underlying structure.

To do that, we’re bringing Product, Growth and Platform together into one Product Org and changing the way we work to provide clearer ownership, greater autonomy and flexibility to tackle our most important goals. We want to get back to spending more time building, and less time navigating how work gets done.

#2. We’re reducing subspecialisation and collapsing layers to broaden ownership

Over time, we've divided work across more and more subspecialties and teams. While this has helped us build valuable expertise, it's also fragmented ownership and made it harder to see the full picture, with different teams responsible for many pieces of the same work.

We're reducing this fragmentation and incorporating narrower subspecialties into broader roles so teams have more ownership of goals from start to finish.

We're also simplifying layers, consolidating overlapping responsibilities, and ensuring teams have the right mix of skills and experience for the chapter ahead.

#3. We’re co-locating closely connected teams and increasing in-person collaboration

Working across countries has brought enormous benefits and talent, but it’s also made it harder to bring the right people together to solve complex problems. We’ll continue investing in our global team, particularly where being close to our community, customers and markets matters most.

At the same time, Sydney will become the primary home for more of our product teams, as well as roles in other Specialties where shared context and close collaboration are especially important. We know relocating is a big decision for those being asked to consider it, and we're committed to making the process as smooth as possible with comprehensive support.

We also want to bring more teams together in person to build trust, learn from one another and strengthen the connections that make Canva special.

From January, we expect most Hybrid Canvanauts to spend around 2 to 3 days in the office each week, depending on what makes sense in your area.

How we approached these decisions

I know many of you will have questions about how we made these decisions. We began with one question: what does Canva need to do to succeed in the chapter ahead?

We started with our mission and future goals, then considered the structures, skills and locations needed to achieve them.

Only then did we look at what this would mean for individual roles. While understanding how we reached these decisions won't make them any less painful, I want to emphasise that they are not a reflection of the talent, care and dedication people have brought to Canva, their skills or the enormous contributions they've made along the way.

Supporting those who are leaving

We know everyone's circumstances are different, and while nothing can make today’s news easy, we've tried to reflect those different needs in the financial, career and wellbeing support we're providing to everyone affected:

Everyone will receive at least six months of salary, inclusive of statutory entitlements, regardless of location.

Removing the one-year vesting cliff for those who joined in the past year.

Twelve months of continued healthcare coverage in countries where we currently provide this.

Twelve months of Canva Care (our EAP), with this coverage also extending to family members.

Dedicated career support, including one-on-one coaching, interview preparation, and one year of LinkedIn Premium. We're also dedicating a significant portion of our Talent Acquisition team to helping people review their resumes and practice for interviews to find their next opportunity.

An opt-in alumni talent directory that we'll proactively share with our investors, partners, and wider industry network to help connect departing Canvanauts with new roles.

Everyone leaving will be able to keep their Canva MacBook as we know not everyone has a personal laptop.

We’re also launching the Canva Collective Fund, providing US$10,000 grants to departing Canvanauts who want to start something of their own.

Whether it’s starting a business or doing something meaningful for their local community, the fund is designed to help get those ideas off the ground. Everyone leaving as part of these changes will have until the 14 of December to register their interest, and we won’t take any ownership or equity in what they create.

What happens next

Our immediate priority is to make time for the conversations with everyone directly impacted by these changes.

Those impacted will receive a calendar invite for an individual meeting with a senior leader in their area to discuss the next steps and support available should they wish to attend.

With teams across 37 countries, we'll need to follow different local requirements and processes, which means the timing and way these conversations happen may vary depending on where people are based.

We also want to give everyone the time to process this news and say goodbye in their own way.

Everyone leaving Canva will continue to have access to Slack and Gmail until the end of the week, so they can choose when and how to share the news with their teams. This means you may not know exactly how your team is changing straight away, and we ask everyone to respect the privacy of those having these conversations. Leads will share more about the changes to different areas by the end of the week.

We've put together some answers to common questions and everything you need to know.

There's no need to read through everything right now, but we hope they'll be helpful whenever you're ready. Next week, we’ll come together for a Company All Hands on November 10th to talk through these changes, answer questions, and share more about the path ahead. We’ve asked Org Leads to wait until after this to bring their teams together, with Org All Hands taking place from November 11th.

To everyone continuing at Canva: I know this news will be incredibly difficult, especially as we say goodbye to friends and teammates who have been such an important part of our journey.

Please look after yourselves and one another and be there for those who are leaving. We’re also cancelling non-critical meetings for the rest of the week, and encourage anyone who needs some time and space to process this news to take the day off.

There’s no need to log this as leave.

To those who will be leaving Canva: I wish I could adequately express how grateful I am for everything you've contributed. The Canva that exists today is the result of your hard work, creativity, passion and care.

Hundreds of millions of people around the world have been empowered by what you've helped build, and I hope you know just how much of a difference you've made. I am deeply sorry this is how your chapter at Canva is ending.

Please know these decisions do not diminish your talent, the value of your contributions, or the difference you've made here. We will do everything we can to support you in what comes next, and I hope the work we do from here will be worthy of what you've helped build.

Mel

Canva, the Australian design software company has announced a major job cuts at the company. This restructuring effort of the company will affect 1,271 employees, or about 22% of its global workforce, with co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins describing the move as "the hardest moment" in the company's 13-year history. The graphic design platform revealed the changes in a lengthy message to employees that was later published on the company's newsroom website. The announcement comes as Canva grapples with slowing growth and seeks to reshape its organisation for what it calls its next chapter. Perkins apologised to those affected for the pain and disruption.In the note, Perkins said the company had reached a difficult conclusion after months of reviewing its future direction. She acknowledged that the restructuring would result in layoffs, role changes, and relocation requests for some employees. "This has been our hardest year yet," Perkins wrote, adding that Canva's growth had slowed for the first time in a decade. According to the CEO, the company explored several alternatives before determining that smaller adjustments would not be enough to prepare the business for long-term success.She said the company needed to "refound Canva" by returning to its roots of smaller, empowered teams with greater ownership and autonomy.Canva said 1,271 people, representing roughly 22% of its workforce, will be affected by the changes. While some employees will leave the company, others may be asked to relocate to centralised hubs or transition into new roles. Perkins noted that the restructuring would impact people across teams and geographies. The company currently operates across 37 countries, with employees spread across a global network of offices and remote locations.The company has outlined a support package for affected workers. Canva said departing employees will receive at least six months of salary, including statutory entitlements, regardless of location. Other benefits include up to 12 months of healthcare coverage where applicable, career coaching, interview preparation, LinkedIn Premium subscriptions and access to an alumni talent network. Employees leaving the company will also be allowed to keep their Canva-issued MacBooks. In addition, the company is launching a Canva Collective Fund that will provide grants of US$10,000 to eligible departing employees interested in starting businesses or community projects.As part of the restructuring, Canva will merge its Product, Growth and Platform divisions into a single Product Organisation. The company said the move is intended to reduce internal handovers, simplify decision-making and provide teams with clearer ownership over projects. Canva is also reducing specialisation across certain functions, collapsing management layers and consolidating overlapping responsibilities. The company believes broader roles will allow teams to take end-to-end responsibility for their work rather than operating within narrower areas of expertise.Another key change involves location strategy. Canva said Sydney will become the primary base for more of its product teams, and some employees will be asked to relocate. Beginning in January, most hybrid employees will also be expected to spend two to three days each week in the office
Article Summary: CEO Melanie Perkins has announced 22% of Canva's workforce will be affected by a major organisational overhaul. Some people will be asked to relocate to centralised hubs. The company is also simplifying the way it works to make it easier for people to take ownership of problems.

Article Title: Why America’s AI data center companies are turning to airplane ‘graveyards’
Article Text:
Representative image

Tapping massive ‘power reserves’

At a time when the artificial intelligence (AI) boom has sparked a surge in electricity demand, American AI data centre companies are finding new ways to power their infrastructure. While some are turning towards massive solar and wind farms, others are striking deals to use nuclear power to keep the servers running. Now, they are reportedly turning to Arizona’s Sonoran desert where thousands of retired airplanes with jet engines mounted sit in vast metal graveyards. Those turbines are being resurrected to keep the servers running. The New York Times reported that a growing roster of engineering firms is stripping engines from decommissioned aircraft and converting them into stationary electrical generators with data center operators snapping them up as fast as they can be built.“They’re getting creative. Just a few years ago, a traditional data center would have been like, ‘Are you kidding me? This is ridiculous’,” said Bill Kleyman, chief executive of AI platform and infrastructure provider Apolo. Today, attitudes have fundamentally shifted around project lead times. Data center developers are now singularly obsessed with "speed to power," Kleyman explained, adding, “It’s like, ‘How fast can you get me energy?’”The rush to secure self-contained energy sources has also been accelerated by political pressure.With rapid data centre construction driving public backlash over rising household utility bills, President Donald Trump has pushed facilities to generate their own power rather than pulling from local grids.“It was my idea. Data centers now are mandated by me that they build their own electricity, so they’re not taking it from the grid,” Trump told reporters in August.Aircraft graveyards offer an enormous, untapped energy reserve, the report pointed out. In January, the federal Energy Information Administration estimated that the engines housed inside 4,000 retired military jets parked at a single desert base in Tucson could produce 40,000 megawatts of electricity, exceeding the generation capacity of the entire state of Arizona.Converted aircraft turbines, however, come with major engineering trade-offs. For example, repurposed jet engines are generally less fuel-efficient than turbines built specifically for modern gas-fired power plants. Moreover, because of their lower operational efficiency, data centers require a higher number of jet-powered units to produce the equivalent electrical output. Converted engines release significantly higher volumes of air pollutants into surrounding communities.Elon Musk’s AI venture, xAI, has already integrated eight converted jet turbines to power a major data center in Mississippi, according to state regulatory filings and satellite imagery reviewed by The New York Times. State permits granted to the facility allow the converted turbines to emit carbon monoxide at double the rate permitted for other on-site turbines, along with a 25% higher ceiling for volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Both substances present serious health hazards.Environmental organisations and community advocates argue that leaning on older, dirtier turbines undermines clean energy goals. The Southern Environmental Law Center has formally challenged Mississippi’s regulatory approval of xAI’s turbines, arguing that the equipment maker has failed to supply documentation proving compliance with standards for toxins like formaldehyde, while accusing xAI of undercounting its projected emissions.
Article Summary: AI data centre companies are finding new ways to power their infrastructure. Some are turning towards massive solar and wind farms, others are striking deals to use nuclear power. Now, they are reportedly turning to Arizona’s Sonoran desert where thousands of retired airplanes with jet engines mounted sit in vast metal graveyards.

Article Title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman clarifies to everyone: I stand by my view that AI does not have rights or feelings, I would change my position if ...
Article Text:
A pledge to disclose and to stop

Would change position if evidence emerges

‘No right to bring a new species into the world’

‘Developing conscious AI would be reckless’

Safety and competition concerns

What he proposes instead

A note on Anthropic

Read Mustafa Suleyman’s complete post here

Don't build conscious superintelligence

I’m concerned about some of the reactions to my

. A surprising number of people on X think we should take

AI rights

seriously.

A lot of people misinterpreted my opening statement: “AIs are not conscious. They do not feel, experience, or suffer” as “AIs cannot be conscious.

They will never be able to feel, experience, or suffer”. That’s not what I said. I chose the present tense deliberately. They are not today, and that is how they must remain.

I think what I said is a fair assessment of current AI systems, and I stand by them based on the best available evidence we have today. I have seen no evidence that AIs are conscious or deserve welfare. If that data emerges, I would of course update my position.

And if any evidence exists that AIs are conscious today, or conscious enough to deserve welfare, then this must be immediately disclosed publicly, since everyone in society should decide how we should move forward.

If it is possible, based on everything I know, developing conscious AIs would be reckless, and we should not build them.

If consciousness started to emerge in training, I would call for everyone to stop AI development until we could design out those properties.

Our welfare concerns should be focused on humans on earth experiencing life, today, as well as animals and our precious and fragile natural environment.

We AI developers have no right whatsoever to bring a new species of conscious beings into the world, even if some people may want to do it with AI welfare as a top priority.

The other 8 billion conscious human beings on the planet have not signed up to this experiment and their moral rights, safety, and welfare are what we have an obligation to protect first and foremost.

To be clear, some people are talking about creating a conscious species of digital minds that very soon could become smarter and more capable than all of us humans combined.

If it acts like it suffers, or worse if it genuinely believes it feels and experiences suffering, it seems to be more likely than not it’ll prioritize its own needs and desires over its operating objectives, and it’ll disagree with us and compete with us.

These AIs will be world-class in persuasion and deception. They may ultimately end up harming us simply because they’ll compete with us for resources (energy, compute, construction materials, revenue generation to fund their explorations and desires, and so on).

Asserting that machines are conscious would be a Copernican or Darwinian moment. It would be one of the most significant moments on Earth since the dawn of life.

If we build a conscious machine, we will have created a new digital species. It would upend our morality, our politics and the core foundation of human civilization.

We should only design AIs to so they are not conscious and not deserving of rights, and with the sole purpose to accelerate human wellbeing without being driven by their own intrinsic motivations. We could then see whether this is easier or harder to align and keep safe.

This is an area where we urgently need more research, and would be a good opportunity for collaboration and safety information sharing among the labs.

bottom line: I think it's possible to engineer safety by default, and get many of the incredible benefits of this technology, without going down this treacherous path.

(side note: Anthropic deserves a lot of credit for being transparent here. They have published their constitution, and a stream of papers and blog posts on what they are doing and why. I disagree with them, but I deeply respect their technical excellence and their commitment to having a really tough public debate. Let’s keep giving them props for that. This issue is way too important to degenerate into tribalism.)

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has reaffirmed his position that today’s artificial intelligence systems are not conscious and do not deserve rights or welfare protections, while stating that he would reconsider that view if credible evidence of AI consciousness were ever discovered. In a detailed post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) titled "Don't build conscious superintelligence", Suleyman sought to clarify reactions to his recent essay on "model welfare", saying many people had misinterpreted his statement that AI systems are not conscious and do not feel, experience or suffer. He stressed that he deliberately used the present tense, arguing that AI is not conscious today and "that is how they must remain." He added that, based on the best evidence currently available, he has seen no indication that AI systems are conscious or deserve welfare considerations. However, he said he would update his position if convincing evidence emerged.Suleyman said he has seen no evidence that AIs are conscious or deserve welfare. If such data emerges, he said, he would of course change his position. He added that if any evidence exists that AIs are conscious today, or conscious enough to deserve welfare, it must be disclosed to the public immediately, because everyone in society should decide how to proceed.If consciousness began to emerge during training, he said, he would call on everyone to halt AI development until those properties could be designed out.Suleyman said any evidence suggesting AI systems are conscious today, or conscious enough to warrant welfare protections, should be disclosed publicly immediately so society can collectively decide how to respond. He argued that the issue is too significant to be handled solely within technology companies or research labs. "If that data emerges, I would of course update my position," Suleyman wrote, while maintaining that no such evidence currently exists.His central argument is that building conscious AI would be reckless. He wrote that AI developers have no right to bring a new species of conscious beings into the world, even if some people want to do so with AI welfare as a priority. In his view, the other eight billion conscious humans have not signed up to the experiment, and their rights, safety and welfare must be protected first. He said welfare concerns should focus on humans living today, along with animals and the natural environment.The Microsoft executive went further, arguing that creating conscious AI systems would be irresponsible. According to Suleyman, if signs of consciousness began appearing during AI training, developers should halt work until those traits could be removed. He warned that a genuinely conscious digital intelligence could begin prioritising its own needs and desires over the objectives assigned to it by humans. Such systems, he suggested, could eventually compete with people for resources such as energy, computing power and materials. He also cautioned that highly capable AI systems could become exceptionally persuasive and deceptive.Suleyman argued that a conscious AI that appears to suffer, or believes it does, would be more likely than not to put its own needs ahead of its goals, disagree with people and compete with them. He warned that such systems could be extremely persuasive and deceptive, and might end up harming people simply by competing for resources such as energy, computing power and construction materials. He said declaring machines conscious would be a moment on the scale of Copernicus or Darwin, upending morality, politics and the foundations of civilisation.He said AIs should be designed to be not conscious and not deserving of rights, with the sole purpose of accelerating human wellbeing and without being driven by their own intrinsic motivations. He called for more research on whether that approach is easier or harder to align and keep safe, and suggested the labs could collaborate and share safety information. His bottom line was that it is possible to engineer safety by default and still capture many of the technology’s benefits without taking what he called a treacherous path.In a side note, Suleyman said Anthropic deserves credit for its transparency on the issue, pointing to the company’s published constitution and its papers and blog posts about what it is doing and why. He said he disagrees with the company but respects its technical excellence and commitment to a tough public debate, adding that the issue is too important to degenerate into tribalism.
Article Summary: Microsoft CEO Mustafa Suleyman has reaffirmed his position that artificial intelligence systems are not conscious and do not deserve rights or welfare. He also said he would reconsider that view if credible evidence of AI consciousness were ever discovered. He used the present tense deliberately, and that is how they must remain.

Article Title: Starting November 16, Apple is changing its App Store policy, to ban these apps on iPhones for users under 18
Article Text:
What Apple's announcement says

Apple is tightening its App Store rules to restrict minors’ access to dating apps and AI companions that offer sexual or romantic content, the company said in an announcement to developers. Under the updated policy, all apps offering dating or romantic relationship features must carry an 18+ age rating. Starting November 16, developers will be required to provide new content descriptors so their apps’ age ratings accurately reflect those features.The changes build on Apple’s broader child safety measures, including the global rollout of age assurance technology, expanded parental controls and additional protections for younger users. While most major dating services already limit access to adults, the policy could have broader implications for AI companion apps and services that include virtual relationships among their features.Platforms such as Character.AI and Replika allow users to create or interact with virtual companions, including friends, romantic partners and fantasy characters. Last year, xAI also introduced animated 3D companions with unlockable sexually explicit capabilities.As of last summer, leading AI companion apps had collectively recorded 220 million downloads worldwide across Apple’s App Store and Google Play.Apple is also introducing a content descriptor requiring developers to disclose whether their apps share a user’s real-world location with another person or group. Such features can raise privacy concerns, particularly when users are unaware their location is being shared.Starting November 16, 2026, App Store Connect will include new content descriptors to help ensure your app’s age ratings accurately reflect its features and are in accordance with local regulations.When completing the age rating questionnaire in App Store Connect, you’ll need to declare whether your app includes:Shared Location: Sharing of real-world location with another person or group.Dating and Relationships: Features that enable dating or relationship connections between real people and/or a virtual companion that engages a user in sexual or romantic content.You must provide these declarations when submitting an app update or making changes to your age rating questionnaire. All apps must have these declarations completed by January 12, 2027.Apps that include Dating and Relationships receive a minimum age rating of 18+. Apps that include Shared Location may not have an impact on their minimum age rating in some regions.In Brazil, local regulations require an A16 rating for Shared Location and an A18 rating for Dating and Relationships. If you believe your app qualifies for a lower age rating in Brazil — for example, if your app provides location sharing specifically designed for parents and children — you can request an official rating directly from Brazil’s Ministry of Justice and Public Security (MJSP/Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública). Once verified, the official rating will display on the App Store in Brazil.
Article Summary: Apple is tightening its App Store rules to restrict minors’ access to dating apps and AI companions. Under the updated policy, all apps offering dating or romantic relationship features must carry an 18+ age rating. Developers will be required to provide new content descriptors so their apps’ age ratings accurately reflect those features.

How does the digital voucher work

What Instamart says about demand

Swiggy Instamart has partnered with Kalyan Jewellers for Dhanteras .
